paragraphs: Hyman cites Yevamot 8a and [Horayot 8a](https://www.sefaria.org/Horayot.8a.17) for Rav Chilkiyah of Hagronia’s objection, “The reason is that the Merciful One wrote…,” etc.[^3]

notes.text: The matching William Davidson digital passage at Horayot 8a has Rav Chilkiyah of Hagronia objecting with טעמא דלא חלק הכתוב. Hyman’s quotation טעמא דכתב רחמנא is retained in the translation. The additional Yevamot 8a citation remains unlocated; no whole-folio or edition-wide absence is asserted from the saved Horayot passage.

Hyman’s printed page cites Yevamot 8a. The wording he quotes occurs in Yevamot 9a, where Rav Chilkiyah of Hagronia asks what offering the community could otherwise bring. In the parallel on Horayot 8a, his objection begins, “The reason is that the verse did not distinguish.”

[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1338&lang=en) cites [Yevamot 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.9a.15) and Horayot 8a. In Yevamot, Rav Chilkiyah’s objection starts from the phrase “one law,” whereas in Horayot it starts from the verse’s lack of a distinction. Hyman’s quoted wording matches the Yevamot form.
